001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
004import java.lang.ref.WeakReference;
005import java.time.Instant;
006import java.util.ArrayList;
007import java.util.Set;
008import java.util.stream.Collectors;
009
010import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
011
012import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor;
013import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source;
014import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.CaseChanging;
015
016/**
017 * A dynamic version of {@link LogEvent}'s static "<code>of</code>" factory methods - same
018 * method shapes (level, message, ...), but {@link #timestamp()}, {@link #threadName()},
019 * {@link #threadId()} and {@link #loggerName()} are resolved through overridable methods
020 * instead of being passed in on every call/pulled from
021 * {@link Instant#now()}/{@link Thread#currentThread()} inline the way those static
022 * methods do. Those static methods are unaffected for now; this is a first step toward
023 * eventually replacing them.
024 * <p>
025 * Not being able to override thread name/thread id/timestamp is a real limitation for
026 * anything that needs deterministic events not tied to whichever real thread happens to
027 * construct them - tests especially, but possibly other reasons later. A test-specific
028 * implementation overriding those methods once gets an entire family of
029 * event-construction methods that are deterministic, rather than needing to thread fixed
030 * values through every call site.
031 * <p>
032 * Each arity of message argument has its own, distinctly-named method
033 * ({@link #eventNoArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Throwable) eventNoArg}/
034 * {@link #eventOneArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Object) eventOneArg}/
035 * {@link #eventTwoArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Object, Object) eventTwoArg}/
036 * {@link #eventArgs(Level, String, KeyValues, Object[], Throwable) eventArgs}) rather
037 * than being overloaded under one name and disambiguated only by parameter shape - this
038 * is meant to be the one place any facade implementation (SLF4J, JCL, JUL, ...) goes to
039 * build events correctly, and overload resolution across five-plus differently-shaped
040 * methods sharing a name reads confusingly at call sites once there are this many of
041 * them.
042 * <p>
043 * This holds no mutable per-instance state - implementations are expected to be immutable
044 * too. Implement it (or extend {@link #of(String)}'s returned instance's behavior by
045 * writing your own implementation) and override individual methods to customize how
046 * events get constructed.
047 *
048 * @apiNote a builder that in turn builds/configures a factory was considered but is not
049 * included (yet) - implementing this directly covers today's need (mainly tests and
050 * facade modules) with less machinery.
051 */
052public interface LogEventFactory {
053
054        /**
055         * Creates a factory bound to the given logger name, otherwise using default behavior
056         * for {@link #timestamp()}, {@link #threadName()}, {@link #threadId()} and
057         * {@link #messageFormatter()}.
058         * @param loggerName logger name every event created by the returned factory will
059         * have.
060         * @return factory.
061         */
062        public static LogEventFactory of(String loggerName) {
063                return new DefaultLogEventFactory(loggerName);
064        }
065
066        /**
067         * Name of the logger every event created by this factory will have.
068         * @return logger name.
069         */
070        String loggerName();
071
072        /**
073         * Timestamp to use for the next event created by this factory. Default is
074         * {@link Instant#now()}.
075         * @return timestamp.
076         */
077        default Instant timestamp() {
078                return Instant.now();
079        }
080
081        /**
082         * Thread name to use for the next event created by this factory. Default is
083         * {@link Thread#getName() Thread.currentThread().getName()}.
084         * @return thread name.
085         * @apiNote this maybe empty and often is if virtual threads are used.
086         */
087        default String threadName() {
088                return Thread.currentThread().getName();
089        }
090
091        /**
092         * Thread id to use for the next event created by this factory. Default is
093         * {@link Thread#threadId() Thread.currentThread().threadId()}.
094         * @return thread id.
095         */
096        default long threadId() {
097                return Thread.currentThread().threadId();
098        }
099
100        /**
101         * Key values to use for the next event created by this factory when a caller does not
102         * supply an explicit {@link KeyValues}. Default is every {@link KeyValuesContributor}
103         * registered with the currently bound {@link RainbowGum} merged together (see
104         * {@link KeyValuesContributor#global(KeyValuesContributor.Source...)}), which is
105         * empty if none are registered or no Rainbow Gum is bound.
106         * @return key values.
107         */
108        default KeyValues defaultKeyValues() {
109                return KeyValuesContributors.GLOBAL.keyValues();
110        }
111
112        /**
113         * Formatter to use for rendering a message when
114         * {@link LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder)} is called on events created by
115         * this factory that take arguments. Default is
116         * {@link LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter#SLF4J}.
117         * @return message formatter.
118         * @apiNote a method rather than a parameter on the {@code eventXxx} methods below
119         * since this rarely changes per event - override it instead if a different formatter
120         * is needed.
121         */
122        default LogMessageFormatter messageFormatter() {
123                return LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter.SLF4J;
124        }
125
126        /**
127         * Creates a log event whose message is already formatted (no arguments). Corresponds
128         * to
129         * {@link LogEvent#of(Instant, String, long, Level, String, String, KeyValues, Throwable)}.
130         * @param level the logging level.
131         * @param formattedMessage the unformatted message.
132         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
133         * @param throwable an exception if passed maybe <code>null</code>.
134         * @return event.
135         * @apiNote the message is already assumed to be formatted as no arguments are passed.
136         */
137        default LogEvent eventNoArg(Level level, @Nullable String formattedMessage, KeyValues keyValues,
138                        @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
139                return LogEvent.of(timestamp(), threadName(), threadId(), level, loggerName(), formattedMessage, keyValues,
140                                throwable);
141        }
142
143        /**
144         * Like {@link #eventNoArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Throwable)} but using
145         * {@link #defaultKeyValues()}.
146         * @param level the logging level.
147         * @param formattedMessage the unformatted message.
148         * @param throwable an exception if passed maybe <code>null</code>.
149         * @return event.
150         */
151        default LogEvent eventNoArg(Level level, @Nullable String formattedMessage, @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
152                return eventNoArg(level, formattedMessage, defaultKeyValues(), throwable);
153        }
154
155        /**
156         * Creates a log event with a single message argument. Corresponds to
157         * {@link LogEvent#ofOneArg(Instant, String, long, Level, String, String, KeyValues, LogMessageFormatter, Object)}.
158         * @param level the logging level.
159         * @param message the unformatted message.
160         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
161         * @param arg1 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
162         * @return event.
163         */
164        default LogEvent eventOneArg(Level level, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues, @Nullable Object arg1) {
165                Instant timestamp = timestamp();
166                String threadName = threadName();
167                long threadId = threadId();
168                String loggerName = loggerName();
169                var messageFormatter = messageFormatter();
170                return LogEvent.ofOneArg(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
171                                messageFormatter, arg1);
172        }
173
174        /**
175         * Like {@link #eventOneArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Object)} but using
176         * {@link #defaultKeyValues()}.
177         * @param level the logging level.
178         * @param message the unformatted message.
179         * @param arg1 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
180         * @return event.
181         */
182        default LogEvent eventOneArg(Level level, @Nullable String message, @Nullable Object arg1) {
183                return eventOneArg(level, message, defaultKeyValues(), arg1);
184        }
185
186        /**
187         * Creates a log event with two message arguments. Corresponds to
188         * {@link LogEvent#ofTwoArgs(Instant, String, long, Level, String, String, KeyValues, LogMessageFormatter, Object, Object)}.
189         * @param level the logging level.
190         * @param message the unformatted message.
191         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
192         * @param arg1 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
193         * @param arg2 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
194         * @return event.
195         */
196        default LogEvent eventTwoArg(Level level, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues, @Nullable Object arg1,
197                        @Nullable Object arg2) {
198                Instant timestamp = timestamp();
199                String threadName = threadName();
200                long threadId = threadId();
201                String loggerName = loggerName();
202                var messageFormatter = messageFormatter();
203                return LogEvent.ofTwoArgs(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
204                                messageFormatter, arg1, arg2);
205        }
206
207        /**
208         * Like {@link #eventTwoArg(Level, String, KeyValues, Object, Object)} but using
209         * {@link #defaultKeyValues()}.
210         * @param level the logging level.
211         * @param message the unformatted message.
212         * @param arg1 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
213         * @param arg2 argument that will be passed to {@link #messageFormatter()}.
214         * @return event.
215         */
216        default LogEvent eventTwoArg(Level level, @Nullable String message, @Nullable Object arg1, @Nullable Object arg2) {
217                return eventTwoArg(level, message, defaultKeyValues(), arg1, arg2);
218        }
219
220        /**
221         * Creates a log event with an array of message arguments. Corresponds to
222         * {@link LogEvent#ofAll(Instant, String, long, Level, String, String, KeyValues, Throwable, LogMessageFormatter, Object[])}.
223         * @param level the logging level.
224         * @param message the unformatted message.
225         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
226         * @param args an array of arguments that will be passed to
227         * {@link #messageFormatter()}. The contents maybe null elements but the array itself
228         * should not be null.
229         * @param throwable an exception if passed maybe <code>null</code>.
230         * @return event.
231         */
232        default LogEvent eventArgs(Level level, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues,
233                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args, @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
234                return LogEvent.ofAll(timestamp(), threadName(), threadId(), level, loggerName(), message, keyValues, throwable,
235                                messageFormatter(), args);
236        }
237
238        /**
239         * Like {@link #eventArgs(Level, String, KeyValues, Object[], Throwable)} with no
240         * throwable.
241         * @param level the logging level.
242         * @param message the unformatted message.
243         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
244         * @param args an array of arguments that will be passed to
245         * {@link #messageFormatter()}.
246         * @return event.
247         */
248        default LogEvent eventArgs(Level level, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues,
249                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args) {
250                return eventArgs(level, message, keyValues, args, null);
251        }
252
253        /**
254         * Like {@link #eventArgs(Level, String, KeyValues, Object[], Throwable)} but using
255         * {@link #defaultKeyValues()}.
256         * @param level the logging level.
257         * @param message the unformatted message.
258         * @param args an array of arguments that will be passed to
259         * {@link #messageFormatter()}.
260         * @param throwable an exception if passed maybe <code>null</code>.
261         * @return event.
262         */
263        default LogEvent eventArgs(Level level, @Nullable String message,
264                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args, @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
265                return eventArgs(level, message, defaultKeyValues(), args, throwable);
266        }
267
268        /**
269         * Like {@link #eventArgs(Level, String, KeyValues, Object[], Throwable)} but using
270         * {@link #defaultKeyValues()} and no throwable.
271         * @param level the logging level.
272         * @param message the unformatted message.
273         * @param args an array of arguments that will be passed to
274         * {@link #messageFormatter()}.
275         * @return event.
276         */
277        default LogEvent eventArgs(Level level, @Nullable String message,
278                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args) {
279                return eventArgs(level, message, defaultKeyValues(), args, null);
280        }
281
282        /**
283         * A source of ambient key values (MDC like context) for events whose logging API has
284         * no context of its own, such as JUL or {@link System.Logger}. Each supported store
285         * of ambient key values registers one with
286         * {@link #register(ServiceRegistry, Source, KeyValuesContributor)}, usually from a
287         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator}.
288         * <p>
289         * Only the stores listed in {@link Source.Standard} can contribute. When more than
290         * one is registered they are merged in the declaration order of
291         * {@link Source.Standard}, so on a key collision the later constant wins. A logging
292         * facade that has its own context store excludes its own {@link Source} when
293         * resolving the rest and passes its own key values to {@link #keyValues(KeyValues)},
294         * which places them above every other source except {@link Source.Standard#USER}.
295         *
296         * <p>
297         * {@link #clear()} clears the current thread's context in every store, for example
298         * when a pooled thread finishes a task:
299         * {@snippet :
300         * KeyValuesContributor.global().clear();
301         * }
302         * Appender buffers kept per thread are cleared separately with
303         * {@link LogAppender#clearThreadLocals()}.
304         *
305         * @apiNote Rainbow Gum core deliberately has no API for putting key values into a
306         * context. Contributors only expose (and clear) whatever context store the
307         * application already uses.
308         */
309        @FunctionalInterface
310        public interface KeyValuesContributor {
311
312                /**
313                 * Key values for an event being created on the current thread. Called once per
314                 * event on the logging thread so it should be cheap. It must not throw or log and
315                 * should return {@link KeyValues#of()} when there is nothing to contribute. The
316                 * returned key values may be live (not a copy) as long as they are not modified
317                 * while the event is being created.
318                 * @return key values, never {@code null}.
319                 */
320                KeyValues keyValues();
321
322                /**
323                 * Like {@link #keyValues()} but with a logging facade's own key values merged in
324                 * above every contributor except {@link Source.Standard#USER}, which still wins.
325                 * @param own the calling facade's own context, for example its MDC.
326                 * @return merged key values, which is {@code own} itself when nothing else
327                 * contributes.
328                 */
329                default KeyValues keyValues(KeyValues own) {
330                        return KeyValues.merge(keyValues(), own);
331                }
332
333                /**
334                 * Clears all of the current thread's state in the underlying context store,
335                 * including state that is not exposed as key values such as a nested diagnostic
336                 * context (NDC) stack, so a pooled thread starts its next task with no context
337                 * left over. A store that cannot be cleared this way, such as one bound to a
338                 * scope, does nothing. Like {@link #keyValues()} it must not throw or log. The
339                 * default does nothing.
340                 * @see LogAppender#clearThreadLocals()
341                 */
342                default void clear() {
343                }
344
345                /**
346                 * Identifies a context store that contributes key values.
347                 *
348                 * @apiNote sealed so that contributions come only from known stores: an unknown
349                 * third party contributor could silently change or break the key values of every
350                 * event.
351                 */
352                public sealed interface Source permits Source.Standard {
353
354                        /**
355                         * The context stores Rainbow Gum supports, in merge order: a later constant
356                         * wins over an earlier one on a key collision.
357                         */
358                        @CaseChanging
359                        enum Standard implements Source {
360
361                                /**
362                                 * {@code rainbowgum-scopedkeyvalues} ({@code ScopedKeyValues}).
363                                 */
364                                SCOPED_KEY_VALUES,
365                                /**
366                                 * {@code rainbowgum-jboss-logging} ({@code org.jboss.logging.MDC}).
367                                 */
368                                JBOSS_LOGGING,
369                                /**
370                                 * {@code rainbowgum-log4j2}
371                                 * ({@code org.apache.logging.log4j.ThreadContext}).
372                                 */
373                                LOG4J2,
374                                /**
375                                 * {@code rainbowgum-slf4j} ({@code org.slf4j.MDC}).
376                                 */
377                                SLF4J,
378                                /**
379                                 * The application's own contributor, which wins over every other source
380                                 * including a logging facade's own context store. Only for applications:
381                                 * a library must not register a {@code USER} contributor, since there is
382                                 * only one per Rainbow Gum and the application decides what it is.
383                                 */
384                                USER;
385
386                        }
387
388                }
389
390                /**
391                 * Registers the contributor for a context store. A store that is already
392                 * registered is not replaced.
393                 * @param registry usually {@link LogConfig#serviceRegistry()}.
394                 * @param source which context store the contributor exposes.
395                 * @param contributor the contributor.
396                 */
397                public static void register(ServiceRegistry registry, Source source, KeyValuesContributor contributor) {
398                        registry.put(KeyValuesContributor.class, KeyValuesContributors.registryName(source), contributor);
399                }
400
401                /**
402                 * Combines the contributors currently registered in a service registry, skipping
403                 * the excluded sources. The registry is read once on this call, so contributors
404                 * registered afterward are not included.
405                 * @param registry where contributors are registered.
406                 * @param excluded sources to skip, usually the caller's own.
407                 * @return combined contributor, which returns {@link KeyValues#of()} if nothing
408                 * is registered.
409                 */
410                public static KeyValuesContributor of(ServiceRegistry registry, Source... excluded) {
411                        return KeyValuesContributors.of(registry, Set.of(excluded));
412                }
413
414                /**
415                 * Combines the contributors registered with whichever {@link RainbowGum} is bound
416                 * globally at the time key values are requested, skipping the excluded sources.
417                 * Meant for logging facades that route through {@link LogRouter#global()} and so
418                 * cannot hold a reference to a particular Rainbow Gum.
419                 * @param excluded sources to skip, usually the caller's own.
420                 * @return contributor that follows the globally bound Rainbow Gum and returns
421                 * {@link KeyValues#of()} while none is bound.
422                 */
423                public static KeyValuesContributor global(Source... excluded) {
424                        if (excluded.length == 0) {
425                                return KeyValuesContributors.GLOBAL;
426                        }
427                        return new KeyValuesContributors.Global(Set.of(excluded));
428                }
429
430        }
431
432}
433
434record DefaultLogEventFactory(String loggerName) implements LogEventFactory {
435}
436
437final class KeyValuesContributors {
438
439        static final Global GLOBAL = new Global(Set.of());
440
441        private KeyValuesContributors() {
442        }
443
444        static String registryName(Source source) {
445                return switch (source) {
446                        case Source.Standard s -> s.name();
447                };
448        }
449
450        static KeyValuesContributor of(ServiceRegistry registry, Set<Source> excluded) {
451                var below = new ArrayList<KeyValuesContributor>();
452                KeyValuesContributor user = null;
453                for (var source : Source.Standard.values()) {
454                        if (excluded.contains(source)) {
455                                continue;
456                        }
457                        var c = registry.findOrNull(KeyValuesContributor.class, registryName(source));
458                        if (c == null) {
459                                continue;
460                        }
461                        if (source == Source.Standard.USER) {
462                                user = c;
463                        }
464                        else {
465                                below.add(c);
466                        }
467                }
468                if (below.isEmpty() && user == null) {
469                        return Empty.INSTANCE;
470                }
471                return new Composite(below.toArray(new KeyValuesContributor[0]), user);
472        }
473
474        enum Empty implements KeyValuesContributor {
475
476                INSTANCE;
477
478                @Override
479                public KeyValues keyValues() {
480                        return KeyValues.of();
481                }
482
483                @Override
484                public KeyValues keyValues(KeyValues own) {
485                        return own;
486                }
487
488        }
489
490        /*
491         * Merge order, lowest first: the non USER contributors in Source.Standard order, the
492         * caller's own key values, then USER.
493         */
494        static final class Composite implements KeyValuesContributor {
495
496                private final KeyValuesContributor[] below;
497
498                private final @Nullable KeyValuesContributor user;
499
500                Composite(KeyValuesContributor[] below, @Nullable KeyValuesContributor user) {
501                        this.below = below;
502                        this.user = user;
503                }
504
505                @Override
506                public KeyValues keyValues() {
507                        return keyValues(KeyValues.of());
508                }
509
510                @Override
511                public KeyValues keyValues(KeyValues own) {
512                        KeyValues result = KeyValues.of();
513                        for (var c : below) {
514                                result = KeyValues.merge(result, c.keyValues());
515                        }
516                        result = KeyValues.merge(result, own);
517                        var u = user;
518                        if (u != null) {
519                                result = KeyValues.merge(result, u.keyValues());
520                        }
521                        return result;
522                }
523
524                @Override
525                public void clear() {
526                        for (var c : below) {
527                                c.clear();
528                        }
529                        var u = user;
530                        if (u != null) {
531                                u.clear();
532                        }
533                }
534
535        }
536
537        /*
538         * Resolves the registered contributors once per bound gum instead of per event. The
539         * registry is complete by the time a gum is bound since configurators run before.
540         */
541        static final class Global implements KeyValuesContributor {
542
543                private record Resolved(RainbowGum gum, KeyValuesContributor contributor) {
544                }
545
546                private final Set<Source> excluded;
547
548                private final String registryName;
549
550                private volatile WeakReference<Resolved> resolved = new WeakReference<>(null);
551
552                Global(Set<Source> excluded) {
553                        this.excluded = excluded;
554                        this.registryName = excluded.stream()
555                                .map(KeyValuesContributors::registryName)
556                                .sorted()
557                                .collect(Collectors.joining(","));
558                }
559
560                @Override
561                public KeyValues keyValues() {
562                        return contributor().keyValues();
563                }
564
565                @Override
566                public KeyValues keyValues(KeyValues own) {
567                        return contributor().keyValues(own);
568                }
569
570                @Override
571                public void clear() {
572                        contributor().clear();
573                }
574
575                @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality") // identity of the bound gum is the point
576                private KeyValuesContributor contributor() {
577                        var gum = RainbowGumHolder.peek();
578                        if (gum == null) {
579                                return Empty.INSTANCE;
580                        }
581                        var r = resolved.get();
582                        if (r == null || r.gum() != gum) {
583                                var registry = gum.config().serviceRegistry();
584                                /*
585                                 * The gum owns the strong reference, so an idle global contributor cannot
586                                 * retain a closed gum or its context stores. While bound, the weak cache
587                                 * stays live and avoids a registry lookup on every event.
588                                 */
589                                r = registry.putIfAbsent(Resolved.class, registryName, () -> new Resolved(gum, of(registry, excluded)));
590                                resolved = new WeakReference<>(r);
591                        }
592                        return r.contributor();
593                }
594
595        }
596
597}
